extracted.intended_audience: academics, researchers and practitioners in cryptocurrency finance, network science, and systemic risk analysis
extracted.subtask_description: A quantitative, data-driven case study analysing the causes and market effects of FTX's November 2022 failure using hourly prices, on-chain data and transaction-level trades, and network-science methods to model dependency structures among cryptocurrencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of heterogeneous data sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Use three heterogeneous data sources: hourly closing prices, on-chain data and public transaction data to analyse events at different granularities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine these data to cross-validate findings: hourly prices for market-level dynamics, on-chain for reserves/ownership insights, and transaction-level trades for immediate microstructure (selling/buying pressure). The paper frames this as a threefold contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hourly USD closing prices from liquid exchange (Binance) via CCXT
rubrics_metrics.description: Use hourly USD closing prices for 199 cryptocurrencies obtained from Binance through the CCXT Python package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select liquid exchanges and traded data to guarantee reliability (citing Alexander and Dakos). Use rescaled hourly closing prices and mark event timestamps on plots. The paper uses a 24-hour rolling window with 1-hour steps for correlations.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-chain data for reserves and structural evidence (Glassnode)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use high-quality on-chain data (Glassnode) to measure reserves held in BTC and ETH and other on-chain metrics to validate events reconstruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare reserves evolution across exchanges (e.g., FTX vs Binance) and use on-chain evidence to support claims about asset sales or liquidity drains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transaction-level trade data and computation of imbalances
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain public trades from Binance (via CCXT) expressed in BUSD and compute minute-level imbalances to detect selling/buying pressure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: separate buy and sell trades, compute transaction cost per trade as volume * execution price, aggregate transaction costs by minute, subtract total buy costs from total sell costs to obtain imbalance. Plot minutely imbalances (positive = selling pressure, negative = buying pressure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Event timeline reconstruction and timestamp mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a detailed timeline of relevant events (e.g., Terra-Luna collapse, CoinDesk report, Binance announcement to liquidate FTT, CEO tweets, Binance non-binding letter, bankruptcy filing) with precise dates/times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the timeline to align market metrics (prices, imbalances, correlations, centrality) with specific events and interpret causal relationships while distinguishing conjecture from evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exponentially smoothed weighted Pearson correlation
rubrics_metrics.description: Model linear relationships among assets with a Pearson correlation coefficient weighted with exponential smoothing: rho_{i,j}^w with weights w_t = w_0 e^{(t-Δt)/θ} and sum_{t=1}^{Δt} w_t = 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rolling windows of Δt = 24 hours with 1-hour steps and set θ = 0.1 (results claimed consistent for different θ). Exponential weighting gives more weight to recent observations and mitigates sensitivity during stress periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triangulated Maximally Filtered Graph (TMFG) for dependency modelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Use TMFG as an information filtering technique to model dependencies among cryptocurrencies and to capture meaningful interactions under topological constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TMFG advantages: captures multivariate interactions and provides topological constraints that facilitate regularisation in probabilistic modelling. Use TMFG-derived network as basis for centrality and systemic-impact measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eigenvector centrality to measure time-dependent asset influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure time-dependent influence of each asset within the network structure using Eigenvector Centrality computed on the TMFG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute eigenvector centrality on non-overlapping 24-hour windows (the paper also shows distribution percentiles across the rest of cryptocurrencies). Use centrality trends to detect abnormal roles of tokens (e.g., unusually high centrality for a utility token suggests misuse/speculation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Buy-and-hold returns (BHR) as performance metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Define Buy-and-Hold Return (BHR) as the relative difference between prices on 01 December 2022 and 01 January 2022 to analyse financial performance of assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use BHR to rank performance, compute median and percentiles (25th, 75th), and to compare ecosystem-level investor trust (e.g., Binance ecosystem vs others).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rolling window choices and resolution (24h windows, 1h steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt rolling windows made of 24 hours with steps of 1 hour each for correlation estimation and 24-hour non-overlapping windows for eigenvector centrality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify window size and step explicitly; justify smoothing/weighting parameters and test consistency across parameter choices (e.g., different theta values).

rubrics_metrics.name: Imbalance/microstructure event detection thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect significant microstructure events by identifying large minute- or hour-level imbalances (e.g., selling pressure spikes of hundreds of thousands to millions BUSD) and link them to public events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report absolute imbalance magnitudes (BUSD) at timestamps and compare to historical maxima (e.g., May 12 2022 highest selling pressure prior to November). Use these magnitudes to support claims about market impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Token-behaviour expectations for utility tokens
rubrics_metrics.description: Expect native utility tokens to be characterised by low market correlation and low degree of centrality by nature; deviation (high correlation/centrality) indicates potential misuse/speculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare distribution of token supply (who holds what share) and its implications: heavily concentrated supply (e.g., 80% held by issuer/insiders) can enable price control and speculative use as collateral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply-distribution and tokenomics scrutiny
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyse token supply distribution (percent held by issuer, foundation, investors, public) to assess fairness of valuation and proper usage as a utility token.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use supply distribution (e.g., BNB: 40% foundation, 10% angels, 50% public) to explain expected lower centrality/correlation. High insider concentration (FTT: 80% held by FTX/Alameda) signals potential for manipulation and fragility when used as collateral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserves analysis across exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare rescaled amounts of BTC and ETH reserves held on exchange addresses (e.g., FTX vs Binance) over the period to detect asset sales and reserve depletion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plot reserve time-series and examine changes after shocks (e.g., Terra-Luna collapse) to support claims about liquidity management and coping mechanisms (selling reserves to cover liabilities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency on data provenance and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Document data sources, retrieval methods and code/packages used (e.g., Binance, Glassnode, CCXT, Defillama, Token Terminal) and provide supplementary material listing all 199 cryptocurrencies with taxonomy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full dataset descriptions (symbols, categories, sectors per Messari taxonomy), exact retrieval dates, and methodological parameters so analyses are reproducible and claims can be independently verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation standards: distinguish quantitative evidence from conjecture
rubrics_metrics.description: When reconstructing causal chains (e.g., Terra-Luna collapse leading to FTT price drop, CoinDesk report and Binance tweets triggering selling pressure), clearly separate observed quantitative signals from conjectured mechanisms (e.g., loan recalls, misuse of customer funds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State conjectures explicitly and support them with converging quantitative evidence (imbalances, reserves decline, centrality shifts) and external reporting; avoid overstating causality where only correlation/temporal association is observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness checks and parameter sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Test consistency of results across different parameter choices (e.g., different θ values for exponential weights) and alternative specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report that main results are consistent under alternative θ settings and discuss any sensitivity; use citations and cross-data validation to increase confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of visualisation conventions to map events to metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Use rescaled plots (prices, reserves, market caps) and overlay event markers (dotted lines at timestamps) to visualise the alignment between news/events and market responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plot multiple series (FTT, BNB, BTC, exchange-average correlation) together to contextualise token-specific behaviour within the broader market reaction. Use color-coding and percentile-shaded areas for centrality distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stablecoin market-share and stability metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure stablecoin supply held on exchanges and rescaled market capitalisation changes (e.g., BUSD share on exchanges, % market-cap change since 01 Jan 2022) to assess shifts toward centralised vs decentralised stablecoins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare top stablecoins (USDT, USDC, BUSD, DAI) on both supply-on-exchange and market-cap dynamics to infer user preference shifts and stability differences (cite relevant literature on correction speeds and stability).
